notes: The write-capable fan-out sign-off now actually closes. The approval card existed, the board showed the fleet, and the refusal named a plan id - but nothing connected them, and the receipt never said WHY a split was worth it. The receipt now carries the complexity band and the roles the clones ran with (as two sub-clauses, so a fleet with no band still reads clean). The fleet board announces a waiting fleet and offers one hop to the approval queue, which highlights the card it lands on. A GET on a plan id now answers 405 with the POST shape instead of pretending a decision can be read. And a real bug fell out of proving this in a browser: POST /api/fleet/plans/<id> was never registered in the POST dispatch - the handler was wired into the GET branch - so the console's APPROVE button could only ever 404. The engine was unit-tested; the route was not. Now registered, and proven end to end by a browser probe: pending plan on the board, hop to the card, row listed, APPROVE turns the row into the approved state. No new credential, no new outbound path.
